howToUseYourJournalAndUnderstandWhatThe: How to use your journal and understand what the numbers can tell you.
takeTwoMinutesAtASimilarTimeEachDay: Take two minutes at a similar time each day. A handful of reliable observations is more useful than a detailed record you cannot sustain.
pickTheLocalDateSelectTheRatingsYouActua: Pick the local date, select the ratings you actually observed, and record sleep and training. Sleep belongs to the date you woke up. Enter actual sleep duration separately from bedtime and wake time: time in bed is not time asleep.
chooseRestDayWhenYouDidNotTrainLeave: Choose <slot0>Rest day</slot0> when you did not train. Leave the training status <slot1>Not recorded</slot1> when you do not know. Blank measurements remain missing; zero is a recorded value. Notes are optional and are not used by the Bayesian model.
bedtimeAndWakeTimeAreLocalClockTimesThe: Bedtime and wake time are local clock times; the app does not infer sleep duration across midnight or daylight-saving changes. Your entry stores an IANA time zone.
theseAreProjectDefinedSelfReportScalesNo: These are project-defined self-report scales, not validated clinical instruments. Use the same interpretation each day; do not change the meaning halfway through a time series.
sleepQuality1VeryPoor10ExcellentSymptoms: Sleep quality: 1 very poor → 10 excellent. Symptoms: 1 mild → 10 severe. Training effort: 1 very easy → 10 maximal. Training pain: 0 none → 10 extreme.
sessionLoadDurationInMinutesPerceivedEff: Session load = duration in minutes × perceived effort. Daily load sums all sessions and is shown in arbitrary units (AU). If any session lacks an effort rating, the whole day’s load is unknown. An explicit rest day has a load of zero.
thisIsASimpleProjectDefinedTrackingHeuri: This is a simple, project-defined tracking heuristic. It is not a validated readiness score and is not comparable across people or necessarily across sports.
forStrengthTrainingAddExercisesWithSetCo: For strength training, add exercises with set count, repetitions, and weight. Group sets only when their repetitions and weight are the same; use another row for a different load.
theModelCombinesAStatedPriorWithYourObse: The model combines a stated prior with your observations. It fits a straight line over calendar time using an exact Normal–Inverse-Gamma conjugate regression. At least 14 non-missing observations of the selected metric are required.
95CredibleIntervalUncertaintyAboutTheAve: <slot0>95% credible interval:</slot0> uncertainty about the average trajectory, conditional on the model. <slot1>95% predictive interval:</slot1> a wider interval for one future observation, including day-to-day variability.
probabilityOfAnIncreasingTrendPosteriorP: <slot0>Probability of an increasing trend:</slot0> posterior probability that the slope is greater than zero. A higher metric is not always better. Forecasts extend at most 28 days from the most recent measurement.
theModelAssumesALinearPatternApproximate: The model assumes a linear pattern, approximately Gaussian noise, constant variance, and independent residuals. Daily health records often violate these assumptions. A residual lag-one correlation is a diagnostic, not a correction.
boundedRatingsAreTreatedAsApproximatelyC: Bounded ratings are treated as approximately continuous. Intervals are deliberately not clipped to the rating scale; boundary warnings make the mismatch visible. Select different priors and date windows to assess sensitivity.
changingDevicesHrvMethodsMissingDaysAndE: Changing devices, HRV methods, missing days, and excluding illness can alter results. Correlation and time trends do not establish cause. This is exploratory self-tracking, not diagnosis or medical advice.
selectYourDateWindowDataGroupsAndFormatW: Select your date window, data groups, and format. Written notes are excluded by default. Dates, time zones, revisions, and timestamps preserve context. JSON, NDJSON, and Markdown include a data dictionary; CSV uses dotted columns and JSON arrays for repeated items.
ndjsonBeginsWithAMetaLineSubsequentLines: NDJSON begins with a <slot0>_meta</slot0> line; subsequent lines are observations. Exports include recorded days only, in ascending date order. Missing days are not invented.
noAiProviderIsConnectedToThisApplication: No AI provider is connected to this application. Exported records are personal data: review your selection before using them elsewhere. Demo exports contain synthetic examples, never your personal observations.
beforeSigningInOpenDemoOrChooseTryDemo: Before signing in, open /demo or choose Try demo on the home or account-access pages. The example journal covers months of running, strength training, sleep, recovery, symptoms and context labels. Dates shift to end today, so the charts and predictions are ready to explore.
tryEveryJournalAnalysisImportAndExportVi: Try every journal, analysis, import and export view. Edits and imports affect only your temporary copy and reset when you leave the demo or reload. Sign in and Create account are available at the top. Signed-in accounts use only their private journal. The demo does not grant account or administrator access.
theRelationshipsWereDeliberatelyConstruc: The relationships were deliberately constructed to demonstrate the tools. They are not observations from a real person or evidence of health effects.
chooseAnOutcomeAndCompareOtherMeasuremen: Choose an outcome and compare other measurements on the same date or 1–28 calendar days earlier. Sleep belongs to the waking date: use a one-day lag to compare yesterday’s training with tonight’s recorded sleep. Daily values, day-to-day changes, detrended values and complete 7/28-day averages answer different questions.
pearsonMeasuresLinearAssociationSpearman: Pearson measures linear association; Spearman measures ranked association. Rankings require at least 14 paired observations. Calendar-block bootstrap intervals need more data and describe sampling uncertainty, not causality. Searching many comparisons can produce large correlations by chance. Check paired counts and compare different windows.
chooseAnOutcomeASameDayOr13: Choose an outcome, a same-day or 1/3/7/14/28-day horizon, and numeric or categorical inputs. Use all recorded dates or a filtered period. Context labels, activities and device categories become explicit binary predictors; written notes are not analyzed.
theModelShowsConditionalAssociationsUnce: The model shows conditional associations, uncertainty and a chronological holdout compared with simple baselines. Sparse or constant inputs are listed with exclusion reasons. All selected inputs must be observed on eligible rows; unknown values are not filled in. A 7-day prediction uses inputs available on its origin date, without inventing future training or sleep.
recordLabelsConsistentlyUncheckedContext: Record labels consistently: unchecked context means unknown, while recording no labels means none applied. Read each feature’s definition and the model diagnostics before interpreting a coefficient as useful predictive evidence.
selectAJsonNdjsonOrCompatibleCsvFileRevi: Select a JSON, NDJSON or compatible CSV file, review its dates and supplied fields, then confirm the destination. Skip existing days preserves saved observations. Merge changes only supplied fields, including explicit nulls; omitted notes remain intact. JSON is the preferred archival format. Markdown and model reports cannot be imported as journal observations.
eachDayHasItsOwnRevisionCheckAndResult: Each day has its own revision check and result. A conflict or interruption can leave a partially completed import. Stop import prevents further rows; a save already sent can finish. Check results before retrying. Files accept up to 500 days / 20 MiB.
createAnAccountWithAnEmailIdentifierAndA: Create an account with an email identifier and a unique password. Email addresses are not verified, and this pilot sends no email. Save your one-time recovery code in a password manager. Recovery and password changes replace the code and sign out older sessions. Account settings also let you sign out or delete your account and journal.
eachAccountCanAccessOnlyItsOwnRecordsThe: Each account can access only its own records. The original owner can use the legacy migration link to keep their existing journal. See Privacy & data for necessary cookies, Cloudflare database storage, retention, and exports.
appearanceOffersLightDarkAndAutoAutoUses: Appearance offers Light, Dark, and Auto. Auto uses sunrise and sunset after you choose Use device location and grant browser permission; without a location it uses a light theme. Approximate coordinates stay in this browser. Update them when travelling or choose Forget saved location. There is no background location tracking. The globe opens language settings: choose manually, or use the saved location for a country-based suggestion. Auto defaults to English without a location. Activities keep fixed English IDs; notes and custom text are never translated.
seeTheDeploymentAndBackupGuideNarrativeF: See <slot0> the deployment and backup guide <slot1/> </slot0> . Narrative fields support up to 50,000 characters each, with a 256 KiB daily request limit. D1 storage is finite; attachments are not supported.
authorizedAdministratorsCanViewAggregate: Authorized administrators can view aggregate account counts, journal volume and recent activity in Administration. This panel contains no individual journal entries or email lists. Read <slot0>about Piotr Żmuda, the author</slot0> and the interests behind the project.
